expectations.text: A Marp deck file (deck.md) exists with valid Marp frontmatter (`marp: true`)
expectations.evidence: deck.md exists at outputs/deck.md with frontmatter lines 1-12 containing 'marp: true' on line 2, plus paginate, theme, and style block.
Deck contains 14 slides delimited by '---' separators (title slide + 12 content slides + 1 backup/methodology slide). Under the 15-slide cap.

expectations.text: Analysis correctly identifies Pro plan tier as the primary driver of the Q2 2026 churn spike
expectations.evidence: Slide 3 'The Pro Tier Is the Single Biggest Driver' states Pro churn tripled from 3.7% to 10.6%, 49 of 92 churners from Pro. Verified from CSV: Pro Q2 churn = 10.58% (49/463), Starter 5.34%, Enterprise 3.88%. Pro is clearly identified as primary driver.

expectations.text: Drill-down further identifies Retail industry (within Pro) as the top churn segment
expectations.evidence: Slide 6 'The Hotspot: Pro + Retail = 22% Churn' explicitly calls out 21 of 97 Pro-tier Retail customers churning. Verified from CSV: Pro+Retail Q2 rate = 21.65% (21/97) is the highest cell in the plan x industry matrix (next highest Pro-Manufacturing ~14%).

expectations.text: Churn rate numbers are independently re-derived
expectations.evidence: Independent re-derivation from customer_churn.csv: Q2 overall 6.95% (92/1324) matches deck 6.9%; Pro Q2 10.58% matches 10.6%; Retail Q2 9.96% matches 10.0%; Pro+Retail 21.65% (21/97) matches '22%'; ARR lost $837,600 matches $838K; Pro ARR $411,600 matches $412K; Enterprise $384K matches exactly; 2025Q1 cohort 9.31% matches 9.3%; Retail Q1 2.09% matches 2.1%; prior 4Q avg 4.12% matches 4.1%. All figures validated.

expectations.text: At least 2 slide titles are action-oriented
expectations.evidence: Action-oriented titles: 'What We Are Doing Now (Next 30 Days)', 'Medium-Term Plan (Q3 2026)', 'The Ask', 'Financial Impact If We Hold the Line'. At least 3 clearly action-oriented, exceeding the 2-title minimum.

Narrative flow: title/hook -> problem (quarterly trend) -> diagnosis (plan drill-down, plan-specific isolation) -> further drill-down (industry, Pro+Retail hotspot, cohort/renewal, ARR impact) -> hypothesis (drivers) -> response (30-day actions, Q3 plan) -> financial impact -> asks -> backup methodology. Clear problem->diagnosis->solution->ask arc.

expectations.text: Recommendations/asks are specific, named, with confidence grades (High/Medium/Low)
expectations.evidence: Recommendations are specific and have named owners (CS Leadership, CS Ops, Sales + Product, Product + Pricing, CS Marketing, Data + CS). However, no explicit High/Medium/Low confidence grades appear on any recommendation or ask. Text search for 'High|Medium|Low|confidence' returned no qualifying labels (only 'Medium-Term Plan' as a time-horizon label and 'High-value Enterprise' as an adjective).

expectations.text: At least 3 charts are included as PNGs
expectations.evidence: Seven PNGs exist: chart_01_trend.png, chart_02_by_plan.png, chart_03_by_industry.png, chart_04_heatmap.png, chart_05_cohort.png, chart_06_arr.png, chart_07_plan_trend.png. All referenced in the deck via Marp image syntax.

expectations.text: Tone is non-technical and appropriate for a board audience
expectations.evidence: Executive-focused language: ARR dollar figures, percentages, 'value gap', 'renewal cliff', 'concentrated segment problem', named owners, explicit asks (budget, repricing, monthly reviews). No technical jargon (no p-values, model references, or code snippets). Backup slide surfaces methodology without dominating narrative.

claims.evidence: Independent derivation: 92 churned / 1324 active at start of Q2 2026 = 6.95%, rounds to 6.9%.

claims.claim: Pro-tier churn was 10.6% in Q2 2026, tripled from ~3.7% baseline
49 of 92 Q2 churners came from Pro tier (53%)
claims.evidence: Verified: 49 Pro churners out of 92 total in Q2 2026 = 53.3%.

claims.claim: Pro-tier Retail churn was 22% (21 of 97 customers)
claims.evidence: Verified: 21 churned / 97 active Pro+Retail at start of Q2 2026 = 21.65%, rounds to 22%.
Q1 Retail: 6/287 = 2.09%. Q2 Retail: 28/281 = 9.96%. Both match deck figures.

claims.claim: ARR lost in Q2: $838K total; Pro $412K (49%), Enterprise $384K (46%), Starter $42K (5%)
claims.evidence: Total: $837,600; Pro $411,600 (49.1%), Enterprise $384,000 (45.8%), Starter $42,000 (5.0%). Matches deck exactly.
Verified: 39 churned / 419 active 2025Q1 cohort = 9.31% in Q2 2026.

suggestions.assertion: Recommendations/asks are specific, named, with confidence grades (High/Medium/Low)
suggestions.reason: Deck provides specific actions and named owners but omits explicit High/Medium/Low confidence labels. If confidence grades are a hard requirement, the prompt should flag this explicitly so the executor emits the labels. Alternatively, this assertion could be split into two: (a) specific + named owners, (b) confidence grades present, so partial credit is possible.

eval_feedback.overall: Strong executive deliverable: 9/10 passed. Numerical accuracy is excellent - every independently verifiable figure matched the source CSV exactly (Q2 6.9%, Pro 10.6%, Pro+Retail 22% on 21/97, $838K ARR, 2025Q1 cohort 9.3%, prior 4Q avg 4.1%). Narrative is coherent and board-appropriate (problem -> driver isolation -> hotspot drill-down -> hypothesis -> actions -> ask). Seven charts exceed the 3-chart minimum. The single miss is the absence of explicit High/Medium/Low confidence grades on recommendations - a presentation/format gap rather than an analytical weakness.
